items.title: Router Security Alert: Thousands of Devices Compromised — Check Yours Now
items.summary:
Thousands of routers and network switches have been hijacked in recent weeks. 
Attackers are exploiting known flaws in Zyxel GS1900 switches and SonicWall 
VPN devices — nearly 1,000 Zyxel switches compromised worldwide, and SonicWall's 
SSL-VPN authentication bypass is being actively abused. CISA added six actively 
exploited vulnerabilities to its must-patch list on November 10, including 
flaws in Cisco BroadWorks and Barracuda email gateways.

What to do: Log into your router or switch admin page (usually 192.168.1.1 or 
192.168.0.1 in your web browser). Check for a firmware update and install it 
immediately. If your device is older than 5 years and no updates are available, 
replace it. Change the default admin password if you haven't already.

items.title: CISA Adds Six Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities — Update Chrome, Outlook, and Barracuda Now
items.summary: CISA added six exploited vulnerabilities on November 10 affecting Google Chrome (CVE-2026-125350), Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194), Barracuda Email Security Gateway (CVE-2026-111560, CVE-2026-116606), Cisco BroadWorks (CVE-2026-20320), and Openwave Webtop (CVE-2026-111793). Update Chrome at `chrome://settings/help`, Outlook via Windows Update, and Barracuda appliances per vendor guidance.

items.title: **Headline:** Windows 11 October Update KB5127648 Breaks Wi-Fi and VPN — Here's the Temporary Fix
items.summary: If your Wi-Fi or VPN stopped authenticating after the October 13 update (KB5127648), open Registry Editor (`regedit`), go to `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0`, set `BlockNtlmv1SSO` to `0`, and restart. This restores Audit mode so legacy NTLMv1-based networks work again. Microsoft warns this weakens security — only use temporarily while IT migrates the network.

items.title: Open Enrollment Scams Are Here — Don't Click That Link
items.summary: Open enrollment season runs through January 15, 2027, and scammers are flooding inboxes and phones with fake health insurance offers. The FCC warns that robocalls and texts pretending to be from "Medicare," "your insurance provider," or "Healthcare.gov" spike during this window. They pressure you to "verify" your Social Security number or pay a fee to keep coverage. Real insurers and government agencies never ask for payment or personal info over an unsolicited call or text. What to do: Hang up. Delete the text. If you need to check your coverage, go directly to Healthcare.gov or call the number on your insurance card. Never use a number or link from the message. Source: FCC.gov — November 1, 2026

items.title: Firefox 160 Stable Released with Mailto Blocking, PiP Speed Controls, and MKV Support — Free at firefox.com
items.summary: Firefox 160 stable was released on November 10, 2026, adding the ability to block websites from repeatedly asking to handle mailto: email links, playback speed controls (0.25x to 2.0x) in the Picture-in-Picture video player, support for Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio, and a Mini Window feature for keeping tabs always on top. Update free at firefox.com or through Firefox's built-in updater.

items.title: Test Suspicious Files Safely in Windows Sandbox — Free Disposable PC Built Into Windows 11 Pro
items.summary: Windows Sandbox gives you a lightweight disposable Windows environment to test untrusted apps, open suspicious email attachments, or visit questionable websites without risking your main system. It resets to a clean state every time you close it. Enable it in Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise via Settings > Apps > Optional features > More Windows features > Windows Sandbox, or run 'OptionalFeatures' and check the box.

items.title: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws Including Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
items.summary: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday addresses 1,235 security vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day in Outlook that steals login credentials when a malicious file is opened. The update also includes fixes for Windows, Office, and Edge. Update now via Settings > Windows Update.

items.title: Windows 11 November Update Adds Cloud Rebuild Recovery and Redesigned Right-Click Menus
items.summary: Windows 11 November update adds Cloud Rebuild recovery, redesigned right-click menus, and fixes for Remote Desktop and printing. Rollout is gradual — check Settings > Windows Update to see if it's available for your device.

items.title: Restart Once a Week to Clear Memory Leaks and Stuck Updates
items.summary: Hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, wait a moment, then turn it back on. This clears memory leaks, stuck updates, and sluggish performance. Do it every Friday and your computer will stay snappy.

items.title: Big Security Updates Today — Microsoft, Google & Apple Released Patches
items.summary:
BIG UPDATE DAY: Microsoft, Google, and Apple released important security updates TODAY to protect your computer from real threats.

Microsoft just released patches for Windows and Office — these fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Google added a new scam protection to Chrome. Apple fixed issues on iPhone and Mac.

What to do: Turn on automatic updates and let them run overnight. You don't have to do anything special. Most updates install while you sleep.

Why it matters: Hackers target computers that haven't been updated. Updates close the doors they try to open.

items.title: Microsoft Released Security Updates for Windows and Office Today — Here's What Changed for You
items.summary: Microsoft released its monthly security updates for Windows 11, Windows 10, Office, and Edge today. These updates fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Let the update run overnight and restart when asked.
